long_biography.plain_text:
For property developer Chad McWhinney, buying farmland from his father was the beginning of a larger land assembly. He moved from Southern California to Loveland at nineteen, then secured options on neighbouring farms while seeking planning approvals. Borrowing against land that had appreciated allowed the brothers to complete their purchases; farming income and rents from farmhouses helped service the debt.

That experience shaped his preference for holding property long enough for development to change its value. At Realberry, he has worked with investors willing to commit capital over long periods, rather than require a fixed timetable for selling. As chairman and chief executive, he directs a business that combines development with investment management, drawing on specialists across different property types.
